title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms for paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We present the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, report bootstrap summaries as descriptive, explicitly label the one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory/post‑hoc, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises reduced manual effort but raises safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and controlled studies document LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that affect code and configuration generation, motivating architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our precise research question is: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics), to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? The design intentionally isolates downstream interventions (validation and at‑most‑one repair) so that any paired difference is attributable to those downstream mechanisms rather than to first‑pass generation differences such as prompt engineering, constrained decoding, or sampling variance.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus and archived validator traces. (2) Full execution accounting and preservable artifacts (preregistration SHA‑256, execution manifest, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis outputs). (3) Transparent confirmatory reporting: exact two‑sided McNemar as the preregistered primary test and bootstrap summaries and exploratory one‑sided results clearly labeled as descriptive/post‑hoc.
sections.related_work:
LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures are documented across recent surveys and controlled experiments; such failures affect code and configuration generation and motivate verifier‑assisted workflows [1],[2]. Constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning have reduced syntactic/executable errors in structured domains, though many demonstrations are outside NetOps and thus depend on validator fidelity when transferred to networking [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system work emphasizes verifier‑assisted repair, guarded architectures, and governance/proof‑carrying proposals; these works present prototypes and argue that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and externally enforced protocols rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Our preregistered paired design complements prior work by isolating the incremental contribution of deterministic downstream validation plus a single limited repair call when the initial candidate is held constant across paired conditions. This avoids conflating downstream interventions with first‑pass prompt/decoding differences and clarifies what the guarded layer alone can achieve under tight control.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The study preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was frozen prior to any hosted‑model invocation (preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Key preregistered elements: paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks drawn from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair deterministically reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) and sensitivity analyses treating failed calls as unsafe.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences. Because generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate both baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled initial candidate; only downstream deterministic validation and the single permitted repair can create paired outcome differences. The design therefore does not measure effects that would arise from independent first‑pass generations, alternative prompts, or constrained decoding arms that were not executed. Any claims about the effectiveness of prompt engineering or alternative generation policies are outside this estimand unless separately executed.

Model/runtime configuration and temperature caveat. The declared provider/model in the archived model configuration is gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The recorded execution/model_configuration.json lists temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The orchestration adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator version 5.0). The deterministic validator enforces sequence/ordering rules, protected‑field noninterference, and required‑command presence and returns a deterministic binary safe‑deploy verdict per task manifest.

Task corpus, validator, and selection. Tasks were selected deterministically by the preregistered ordinal rule producing exactly 1000 unique tasks; each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (very_hard, extreme). The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 compares parsed candidate command sequences against manifest constraints in a digital‑twin emulator and emits archived structured validator traces used for scoring under scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting (artifact‑grounded). The run completed as preregistered (planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0). Provider call audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005 and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}; cross‑condition cache reuse was not observed.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered inferential test. The 2×2 paired contingency table (archived) is n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold, so preregistered H1 is not supported.

Confirmatory vs descriptive hierarchy (preregistered primary vs secondary/exploratory). The exact two‑sided McNemar is the preregistered confirmatory analysis and did not reject at α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.001, 0.01] and is a descriptive secondary summary; bootstrap intervals can exclude zero even when exact tests are non‑significant because resampling with replacement from very sparse discordant counts (here n10=5, n01=0, visible in the archived paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis_log.jsonl) may produce resamples with only positive differences and thus yield a positive percentile lower bound. Any one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) reported here is exploratory/post‑hoc because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration and does not alter the preregistered confirmatory conclusion.

Repair mechanics and representative traces. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred. Representative archived episode artifacts show the validator rejecting initial candidates for required_sequence or protected_interface violations, the adapter invoking the single allowed repair call, and the validator accepting the repaired candidate after revalidation. All raw responses, provider call traces, repair traces (where present), and validator traces are archived and referenced in the execution manifest.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and power mismatch. The preregistered power plan assumed baseline ≈ 0.60 and a target absolute improvement of 0.15; the observed baseline (0.995) diverged substantially from that assumption, producing very few discordant pairs and reducing sensitivity for the preregistered exact paired test. Thus the nonsignificant two‑sided McNemar result (p = 0.0625) should be interpreted in the context of near‑unity baseline validity, not as evidence that validator/repair layers never help in regimes with higher baseline failure prevalence.

Mechanistic implications within shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics only downstream validation and permitted repairs can create paired differences; the five observed repairs demonstrate that a deterministic validator with appropriate rules can correct some ordering/sequence violations. Because repair invocations were sparse, inference about repair efficacy across diverse failure modes is limited and motivates preregistered follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, repair budget, and validator coverage.

Threats to validity and external limits. Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity is strengthened by deterministic seeding and no observed execution failures; external validity is limited by the synthetic corpus and single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini). Conclusion validity is constrained by sparse discordant counts and the discrete nature of exact McNemar in this regime.

Recommended preregistered follow‑ups. (1) Run independent first‑pass generation arms (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure prompt/decoding interventions. (2) Sweep repair budgets to quantify marginal returns per failure class. (3) Expand validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity. (4) Evaluate multiple model families. Each follow‑up should include power calculations aligned to plausible baseline failure rates and preregistered analysis choices.
sections.conclusion:
In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The primary inferential outcome is the preregistered exact McNemar result; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified. Artifact‑grounded evidence shows verifier‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. All preregistration, execution, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with the run to support reproducibility and to guide preregistered follow‑ups.

[1] R. Sapkota, K. I. Roumeliotis, and M. Karkee, "AI Agents vs. Agentic AI: A Conceptual taxonomy, applications and challenges," Informatics Fusion, 2025. DOI: 10.1016/j.inffus.2025.103599.

[2] D. Anh‑Hoang, V. Tran, and L.‑M. Nguyen, "Survey and analysis of hallucinations in large language models: attribution to prompting strategies or model behavior," Frontiers in Responsible AI, 2025. DOI: 10.3389/frai.2025.1622292.

[3] S. Banjade, "Schema‑Constrained LLM Planning for Executable Molecular Workflows: An Intent‑to‑Execution Infrastructure for Cheminformatics," ChemRxiv, 2026. DOI: 10.26434/chemrxiv.15005091/v1.

[4] A. Harrison, "Protocol‑Mediated Execution Governance for LLM Agent Systems," SSRN, 2026. DOI: 10.2139/ssrn.6426760.

[5] J. Augé, S. Betts, G. Carofiglio, G. Grassi, M. Gysi, and J. K. D'Souza, "Aether: Network Validation Using Agentic AI and Digital Twin," arXiv:2604.18233, 2026.

[6] R. Asadli, B. Hoffman, I. Protogeros, and L. Vanbever, "Evaluating Agentic Configuration Repair for Computer Networks," arXiv:2606.06212, 2026.

disclosure_statement: Declared model and provider: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). Orchestration/validator: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Preregistration: cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls; preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Immutable initial master prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). After the autonomy lock the literature review, preregistration finalization, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revisions were performed by the autonomous research run; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
